Brief

A strict markup language for documents written by humans and consumed by humans and LLMs.

View on GitHub Read the spec

Why it exists

Markdown is forgiving — it silently accepts ambiguous input. That is fine for a blog post and bad for documents you feed to an LLM, where every token costs money. Worse, every Markdown product has its own dialect.

Brief refuses ambiguity. Every construct has one canonical spelling, every error has a code, and every document compiles to a deterministic, token-minimized form for LLM prompts.

What makes Brief different

One way to do it

Every construct has a single canonical spelling. *bold*, not **bold**. - for bullets, never * or +.

Compiler-time errors

Ambiguous input is a compile error with a source span and an error code, in the style of rustc. There are no warnings.

Token-economic LLM target

brief compile doc.brf --target=llm produces a deterministic, token-minimized rendering for LLM prompts, with --report-tokens for budgeting.

No inline HTML

The single extension point is registered shortcodes — including the ones that built this page.

Pretty for humans, lean for LLMs

Code blocks compile twice. The HTML rendering keeps your formatting intact. The --target=llm rendering minifies anything safe to minify — JSON in v0.2, C-family languages and SQL in v0.3 — for documents you'll feed to an LLM, where every token is on the bill.

Source
{
  "model": "claude-opus-4-7",
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Summarize the changelog."
    }
  ]
}
--target=llm
{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the changelog."}]}

Same JSON, same semantics, far fewer tokens. Opt out per-block with @nominify when the formatting itself is the lesson.

At a glance

A self-contained example showing most of what Brief offers:

# Release notes

The 0.4 release ships *strict* lists, _italic_ that doesn't fight you,
and a real compiler.

- [x] ship v0.4
- [ ] write release notes
- plain bullet, not a task

@callout(kind: info)
Press @kbd[Ctrl+C] to abort the long-running compile.
@end

Some claim Brief saves tokens.@footnote[Measured against Markdown
on the project's own docs, roughly 25 percent on average.] The compiler can prove it.

Markdown → Brief

Same content, two languages.

Markdown
# Title
**bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~
- one
* two
+ three
Brief
# Title
*bold*, _italic_, ~strike~
- one
- two
- three

Brief refuses the second and third bullet markers — pick one and use it.

Errors look like rustc

Ambiguous input is a compile error, with a source span and an error code:

error[B0204]: emphasis cannot nest with the same marker
  --> doc.brf:14:23
   |
14 | This is *outer *inner* outer*.
   |        ^^^^^^^ inner emphasis re-uses the `*` marker
   |
   = help: use a different emphasis marker for the inner span,
           e.g. _outer *inner* outer_
